newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Consmining surges in speculative trade.
newsitem.headline: Consmining surges in speculative trade.

text.p: Shares in South Africa's Consolidated Mining Corporation Limited (Consmining) jumped to a new year high of 105 cents in heavy volumes on Monday amid speculation about the company's future activities.
The company's stock rose 9.38 percent to 105 cents -- besting its year-high of 101 cents reached on February 13 -- on 4.9 million shares. By 1050 GMT the price had slipped back slightly to 103 cents.
"There's been quite a bit of speculation about Consmining and that's why there has been this heavy volume. We don't know why and what the speculation is about," commented one broker.
Consmining company secretary George Poole declined to disclose details about the company's future activities saying shareholders had to be notified first.

He said Monday's market speculation followed on reports a fortnight ago that Consmining had bought shares in mining house Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd and two gold mines in a bid to enhance its core holdings in the mining sector.
"There has been some developments and there are going to be further exciting developments," he told Reuters.
At the end of January, Consmining said it had bought 590,000 Randgold shares in exchange for 30 million new Consmining shares issued at 70 cents each with effect from December 10, 1996.
It had further acquired 800,000 Randgold shares and 230,000 shares and 175,000 options in Durban Roodeport Deep Ltd and 366,000 East Daggafontein Mines Ltd shares.
"People must be speculating on that," Poole said.
